 Aiden Markram plays a shot as South Africa host Australia in the third Test at Newlands in Cape Town. Follow for live scores and SA vs Aus cricket updates. Follow for live scores and SA vs Aus cricket updates. Photograph: Marco Longari/AFP/Getty Images Geoff Lemon (now) and Rob Smyth (later) Tue 27 Oct 2026 05.35 EDT First published on Tue 27 Oct 2026 03.30 EDT Share Key events 1h ago South Africa XI 
 1h ago Australia XI 
 2h ago Australia win the toss and elect to bowl 
 2h ago Steve Smith to miss third Test 
 2h ago Preamble 
 1m ago 05.35 EDT 14th over: South Africa 53-0 (Markram 31, Ackerman 21) Markram gives up strike facing the first ball from Cummins, but Ackerman immediately gives it back. Still, nothing more ambitious from Markram this over. He’s not been sucked into going too hard with the momentum his way. Drinks. 
 Share 4m ago 05.31 EDT 13th over: South Africa 51-0 (Markram 30, Ackerman 20) Two runs from Lyon’s over, Ackerman knocking the ball through point, but otherwise Ackerman doesn’t look entirely confident in his method against Lyon.
 Share 5m ago 05.30 EDT 12th over: South Africa 49-0 (Markram 30, Ackerman 18) Markram just keeps going. Cummins tries bumping him again, Markram dispatches the short ball for four. This is just a dominant early performance.
 Share 9m ago 05.27 EDT 11th over: South Africa 43-0 (Markram 24, Ackerman 18) It’s Nathan Lyon in the 11th over! That alone tells you that things are not going well for Australia. His comeback over is a decent one, lots of defence from Ackerman, then an ill-judged jump out of his crease for a hoy at the ball, skewed away leg side for a single. Markram scores a more controlled one, down the ground.
 Share 11m ago 05.24 EDT 10th over: South Africa 41-0 (Markram 23, Ackerman 17) This tells you how good this pitch is to bat on. Some width from Cummins, a bit short, but Markram would have been cautious about throwing the bat at Gqeberha where the ball was moving around. Here, angled bat, no hesitation, seared for four.
 Share 21m ago 05.14 EDT 9th over: South Africa 31-0 (Markram 19, Ackerman 16) This is rapidly turning into one of the worst bowl-first decisions ever. So simple for Markram to get onto the front foot and drive that full Starc delivery through cover for four. The Australians of course have the quality to turn things around, but right now, South Africa are right on top.
 Share Updated at  05.23 EDT 23m ago 05.12 EDT 8th over: South Africa 31-0 (Markram 15, Ackerman 15) Oh, my word. The symbolism of this sequence is immense. Cummins brings himself on to bowl. He’s the captain, he’s made the call at the toss, he’s the enforcer when things are getting away from Australia. He’s the one who has to make a statement in his first spell. He bowls a few balls, then drops in his bouncer, and Markram smashes him for six. 
 Clean as a whistle, over midwicket. That’s huge both literally and metaphorically.
 Share Updated at  05.23 EDT 27m ago 05.09 EDT This is perhaps the first recorded link between Andy Zaltzman and Tupac Shakur, but the former has just sent me an email headed Ch-ch-ch-changes! 
 Buckle up for some incredible stats on Australia’s moves.
 double quotation mark “Hi Geoff, hope all is well. You look like the kind of person who would like some pure, unadulterated information about regarding Australia’s four changes.
 If my magic Team Changes spreadsheet is to be believed (and I am almost 101% certain that it is), this is the first time Australia have made four or more changes during a series (i.e. excluding first Tests) since the 4 th Test in Johannesburg in 2017-18. That was the game after S***P****G***. Smith, Warner and Bancroft, plus Starc, were replaced by Burns, Renshaw, Handscomb and Sayers.
 This current Test is only the eighth time Australia have made four or more changes during a series away from home. They also did so twice in India in 2012-13, when four players were naughty-stepped for the 3 rd Test due to the Homework Shemozzle (Watson, Wade and Pattinson, who had played the 2nd Test, plus Khawaja who was in the squad but not playing; Maxwell was also dropped from the XI). The four dropped players, plus Mitchell Johnson, came back into the XI for the 4th Test.
 So the current match is the first time Australia have made four or more changes during an away series without disciplinary intervention since 1994-95, when for the 3rd Test v Pakistan in Lahore, Langer, Emery, May and McGrath replaced S. Waugh, Healy, Fleming and Angel.
 Prior to that, the only times Australia have made 4+ changes during an away series were:
 - the 4th Test in West Indies in 1983-84 (Jones, Woolley, Maguire, Rackemann in for Wood, S. Smith (different one), Hogg and Alderman), and
 - twice in India in 1956-57, when Rutherford, Davidson, Maddocks and Wilson replaced MacDonald, Craig, Langley and Ian Johnson for the second Test, and those changes were reversed for the third Test. (Unusually for that era, those Tests were played back-to-back.)
 The third Test in India in 1956-57 was the only time Australia have won an away Test during a series having made four or more changes.
 Here endeth the stat.
 Share 31m ago 05.04 EDT 7th over: South Africa 24-0 (Markram 9, Ackerman 14) Lyon now at leg slip, but Ackerman pulls wide of him! Gloved that shot, and it could easily have looped up to the catcher, but instead goes a couple of metres wide of him, too much ground to make up.
 Still, choose to bowl first, and by the seventh over you’re trying to take your wickets with a bouncer ploy? It’s not encouraging for the tourists.
 Share 35m ago 05.01 EDT 6th over: South Africa 23-0 (Markram 9, Ackerman 13) Markram punches to point again, but Lyon is stationed right on the white line there and gets in the way. Eventually a leg bye, then a single, from Hazlewood.
 “Given that Cam Green can’t bowl and you have Head, Renshaw and Connolly, this is the test you go in with four seamers,” writes Kevin Wilson. Maybe. There have been some pretty good performances by spinners though on this ground.
 Share Updated at  05.04 EDT 40m ago 04.56 EDT 5th over: South Africa 21-0 (Markram 9, Ackerman 12) Flushed him! Yowch. Starc belts Markram, straight out. Around the wicket, bowls a body-length ball clocked at 149 kph, and that did look quick as well, unlike some of the high readings in the second Test. In at the body and Markram doesn’t have time to do anything but flinch and hope it doesn’t hurt him too badly. It smashes the little wrist guard, but will still have done some damage. Deflects for a leg bye. Ackerman, though, middles his next shot, full on his pads and taken through square.
 Share Updated at  05.00 EDT 44m ago 04.51 EDT 4th over: South Africa 15-0 (Markram 8, Ackerman 7) Hazlewood full again, inside edge again, this one a danger of being played back onto Ackerman’s stumps. He gets going with a leg glance though, four, then drives a single/.
 “Thanks for the coverage again!” writes George van Zijl. “Based on form the Aussies could probably pick Lyon as spinner and include Boland as a batsman. He batted in the top order in both innings last test and did better than most. How many times has a batting pair started two days in a row after a full day’s play? I guess the best bet is when no wickets fall, which only has occurred once in my cricket following days (SA vs Aus at the Wanderers in I think 1996). The Head-Boland partnership should be less unique as bowling a team out and having them follow-on happens more readily than a pair carrying their bats for a full day. Cant wait for this Test.”
 The full-day batting partnership has quite a lot of precedents. Top of my head, Laxman and Dravid in 2001, Taylor and Marsh in 1989, Sangakkara and Jayawardene in the record partnership against your lot, Lara and Jimmy Adams in Kingston. You’re thinking of Steve Waugh and Greg Blewett in 1997. I reckon there would be fewer examples with a team following on, hard to track those without doing it manually though, and I’m a bit busy right now. Anyone free?
 Share 50m ago 04.45 EDT 3rd over: South Africa 10-0 (Markram 8, Ackerman 2) Starc gets Markram hopping and playing from the first ball of the over, but Markram picks off the second, a lovely clip off a leg stump line from a ball that is about hip height, not glanced fine but struck more sweetly square of the wicket. Four.
 Goes again! The sort of shot that has had him in trouble this series, and other players, punching square off the back foot, riding the bounce of a shorter ball to flash it through point, but this time it works perfectly. On a nice sunny morning, is this a batting paradise?
 Share 55m ago 04.41 EDT 2nd over: South Africa 2-0 (Markram 0, Ackerman 2) Hazlewood, by contrast, is on the money immediately. Ackerman has to play at almost everything, and doesn’t look comfortable with the bounce. Wears one on the gloves, squeezes a couple of balls away off the inside edge without control. Survives, though, and picks up two in advertent runs from one of those defensive shots.
 Share 1h ago 04.38 EDT 1st over: South Africa 0-0 (Markram 0, Ackerman 0) Thus begins the day via Mitchell Starc. He was Australia’s champion during the recent Ashes series, then hasn’t had a big influence in the two Tests here so far. Three wickets each during the Durban and Gqeberha matches, produced some good deliveries but had some radar issues.
 His first over here doesn’t correct that, with Markram able to leave the first five balls of the Test.
 Share 1h ago 04.31 EDT So that’s a lot of changes in between preamble speculation and the start of play. Email me your thoughts. Let’s get into it.
 Share 1h ago 04.26 EDT The two teams are on the field at Newlands for the national anthems with first ball only a few minutes away.
 Share 1h ago 04.20 EDT If you missed it, last week Barney Ronay gave his view of Temba Bavuma’s masterwork.
 double quotation mark Bavuma has been a transformative Test captain, with 12 wins in 14 matches, four hundreds, a world championship mace , all stretched over three broken years. But he is still always, always chasing legitimacy and affirmation, in a way that is unique to cricket, but also unique to this man in this role in this sporting nation. First black middle order batsman. First black captain. How is this going to fall? How strong is that ice underfoot?
 Bavuma’s nine-hour masterpiece was art we risk losing in Test cricket’s great purge | Barney Ronay Read more Share 1h ago 04.17 EDT Among the Australia’s four changes for this Test, there’s still no proven replacement opener for Usman Khawaja, who has been on media street lately with his book coming out to coincide with an Australian Story episode.
 ‘Even my best friend didn’t know’: Usman Khawaja reveals why he kept his rheumatoid arthritis a secret Read more Share 1h ago 04.13 EDT South Africa XI
 Aiden Markram, Marques Ackerman, David Bedingham, Temba Bavuma (capt), Matthew Breetzke, Ryan Rickelton (wk), Wiaan Mulder, Marco Jansen, Simon Harmer, Gerald Coetzee, Kagiso Rabada.
 The Proteas are forced to make one change and have no reason to swing any more after their thumping victory by an innings and 31 runs in the second Test. Gerald Coetzee replaces the injured Anrich Nortje.
 Share 1h ago 04.11 EDT Australia XI
 Travis Head, Matt Renshaw, Marnus Labuschagne, Cameron Green, Josh Inglis, Alex Carey (wk), Cooper Connolly, Pat Cummins (capt), Mitchell Starc, Nathan Lyon, Josh Hazlewood.
 Matt Renshaw moves to the top of the order to partner Travis Head with Cameron Green slated to come in at No 4. Cooper Connolly expected to bat after Alex Carey.
 Share 1h ago 04.08 EDT Pat Cummins explains the four selection changes and how close Steve Smith was to playing on Australia’s first Test at Newlands since 2018.
 double quotation mark We’re going to have a bowl, feel like there’s little of moisture in the wicket today.
 [Steve Smith] had another little practice this morning but wasn’t happy with how his neck was feeling. We’ve got some other guys really placed. They’ve been working hard the last couple of weeks, a couple have had injuries, they’re coming back now
 Very hard [to leave out Boland]. He’s such a class player. As it was hard to leave out Nathan Lyon last week, so a good problem to have.
 Share Updated at  04.19 EDT 2h ago 04.03 EDT Australia win the toss and elect to bowl
 Pat Cummins wins the toss and Australia will bowl first against South Africa at Newlands in Cape Town.
 Share 2h ago 04.01 EDT Steve Smith to miss third Test
 Steve Smith has failed a fitness test and with miss the series decider against South Africa in Newlands, as Australia have been forced into a huge change and made a couple more selection calls based on form and fitness. Josh Inglis comes in for the former Australia captain.
 Cooper Connolly will play his second Test in place of Beau Webster, while Australia also turn to Nathan Lyon with Scott Boland the unlucky pace bowler to miss out. Cameron Green returns after recovering from an abdominal strain as the Nic Maddinson experiment comes to an end.
 Share 2h ago 03.55 EDT Australia are expected to make at least a couple of changes. Martin Pegan looked closer at who might be on their way in – and out – of the team.
 double quotation mark The Australian selectors have shown in South Africa they are prepared to change a winning formula with the ball, while they have long been reluctant to cut ties with proven performers with the bat. But the first innings capitulation as Australia were all out for 99 in Gqeberha could force their hand to make a tough call or two – or perhaps more – as a selection storm brews before the series decider in Cape Town.
 Winds of change are coming for Australia as selection storm brews in South Africa | Martin Pegan Read more Share 2h ago 03.50 EDT This was the Australian camp’s attitude yesterday as to whether Smith would be passed fit.
 Australia give Steve Smith chance to prove fitness ahead of South Africa series decider Read more Share 2h ago 03.41 EDT The weather! Always worth checking in this game. Thankfully the forecast suggests that we’ll have less annoyance with rain and light than in the first two Tests, that both got dragged out to five days when better conditions might have had them wrapped up in three or four.
 For Cape Town, the weather is set fair, with sunny days and just some scattered cloud expected. Cool temperatures given the season, low 20s will be the max. Ideal for the players.
 Share 2h ago 03.30 EDT Preamble
 Geoff Lemon One, two, three. That’s as many Tests as we’re going to get in this series, and today begins the third and final. It’s the one that we’ve all been waiting for: the return to Cape Town, the scene of all that went wrong for Australia in 2018, and thus the location with so much riding on it should they put on a performance that would create some fresher and better memories.
 That, though, would require a serious turnaround in form and fortune, given the way South Africa slowly stomped them last week in Gqeberha. Australia’s batting is the weak point, given their win in Durban was largely carried on the capacious shell of The Turtle, Matthew Renshaw, while their loss the following week was down to their insipid 99 all out in their first attempt with the bat.
 We probably already know what the teams will be, pending any late injuries or changes of heart, with minimal changes likely. One batting change for Australia will create a shuffle: Cameron Green back into the side from injury means Nic Maddinson out on lack of runs, with Matt Renshaw moving up to open. Marnus Labuschagne and Beau Webster likely stay put. The other change will be Nathan Lyon in for Scott Boland. Cue debate. There’s some chance Steve Smith will miss with his neck injury, in which case Josh Inglis would likely come in rather than Maddinson shifting down.
 As for South Africa, the injured Anrich Nortje being replaced by fellow fast man Gerald Coetzee is likely the only change, with Temba Bavuma hoping to continue his excellent record as leader, both in terms of wins and of runs.
 Lots going on. Let’s start our walk.
